law: Furigana is the corridor's core teaching surface — the ruby must be TRUE before anything else is. UniDic guesses name readings statistically and shreds rare theonyms; this lexicon carries the human-curated readings for the name compounds the curated shelf actually contains. It is applied at tokenization time (build_corridor.tokenise), proven applied by tools/check_suspect_readings.py, and a reverted build is convicted by verify-native-readings.mjs.

provenance.policy: Token splits stay UniDic's; ONLY readings are overridden, matched on exact adjacent token-surface sequences. Where a deity or person name carries an unwritten genitive の before its final piece, the の attaches to the NAME piece — the same convention UniDic itself already applies to 天之御中主(あめのみなかぬしの) and 太(おおの) — and a name-final 神 token always reads かみ. Readings are hiragana, matching the token 'r' field. A null reading leaves that token untouched (context guard only).

UniDic splits the island name and reads the orphaned 島 with the on-yomi とう (接尾辞), so the shelf's FIRST card taught 屋久やく島とう. The place is やくしま. Every neighbouring place-name in the same sentence — 知床しれとこ半島はんとう, 白神しらかみ山地さんち, 羅臼らうす岳たけ — is already right, so nothing in the surface signalled which one to distrust (E3 round-C, reader lens).

UniDic reads the bare 日本 as にっぽん and tokenizes 日本語 as 日本|語, so the reader printed にっぽん directly above a following 語 at 12 sites across the curated shelf — including token 0 of an N3 graded text, the first word a learner meets there. 日本語 is にほんご; にっぽんご is not a word. The override binds only the adjacent pair, so a standalone 日本 keeps whatever the tokenizer gives it (E3 round-D, reader lens).
